title: Senior's toolkit: CORS, secrets and object-level checks
summary: Test a CORS preflight with curl, configure AddCors, keep secrets in user-secrets and Key Vault, find leaked ones in Git, and check ownership with IAuthorizationService.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: CORS, secrets and object-level checks
steps.body: API security incidents are usually ordinary: a CORS policy nobody tested, a key committed to Git, an endpoint that never checked who owns the invoice. These are the commands and APIs experienced developers use to prevent and spot them.

toolkit.what: Send the preflight a browser would send and read the `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers that come back. Answers "why does the SPA get a CORS error?" in one command.
flags: the site the call comes from
the method the real call will use
toolkit.example: curl -i -X OPTIONS https://api.example.com/invoices/7 -H "Origin: https://app.example.com" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: PUT" -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type"

toolkit.what: Name exactly which origins, methods and headers may call the API from a browser. CORS protects users' browsers; it does not authenticate anyone.
flags: exact origins, scheme and port included
cookies allowed; cannot be combined with `AllowAnyOrigin()`
turn the policy on in the pipeline

toolkit.what: Keep development secrets out of the repository. They are stored in your user profile (plain text, not encrypted) and loaded as configuration in the Development environment.
flags: store a value under a configuration key
toolkit.example:
dotnet user-secrets init
dotnet user-secrets set "Stripe:ApiKey" "sk_test_51Hx..."
dotnet user-secrets list

toolkit.what: Read a secret from Azure Key Vault. Apps read the vault through a managed identity; people use this to check that a value is there and current.
flags: print only the value, no JSON
toolkit.example: az keyvault secret show --vault-name kv-shop-prod --name Stripe--ApiKey --query value -o tsv

toolkit.what: Find every commit that added or removed a string, on every branch. If a secret was ever committed, it is in history: rotate it, do not just delete the line.
flags: commits that change how often `text` appears
every branch and tag, not just the current one
toolkit.when: after a leak report, and alongside a secret scanner such as gitleaks or GitHub secret scanning

toolkit.what: Resource-based authorization: check this user against this particular object (is it their invoice?). The framework's answer to broken object-level authorization.
flags: on failure, often better than 403: it does not confirm the id exists

steps.prompt: The SPA at `https://app.example.com` shows this in the console when it sends PUT with a bearer token. What is the fix?
steps.code: Access to fetch at 'https://api.example.com/invoices/7' from origin 'https://app.example.com' has been blocked by CORS policy: Request header field authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response.
options: Add `authorization` to the policy's `WithHeaders(...)` (and check PUT is in `WithMethods`), then confirm with a curl OPTIONS preflight
Send the token in the query string instead
steps.explain: The preflight asked whether `authorization` may be sent and the answer did not list it. Allow exactly what the SPA needs. Opening everything works but lets any site's scripts call the API from a user's browser.

steps.prompt: Match each preflight request header to what it asks.
pairs: which site the script runs on
which method the real request will use
which extra headers the real request will send

steps.prompt: Store a test API key for local development, then read the production one from Key Vault.
code: az keyvault secret show --vault-name kv-shop-prod --name __2__ --query value -o tsv
steps.explain: Key Vault secret names cannot contain `:`, so .NET's Key Vault configuration provider maps `--` to `:`.

steps.prompt: A live Stripe key was committed to a public repository an hour ago. Put the response in order.
lines: Revoke the key at Stripe and issue a new one
Store the new key in Key Vault and redeploy
Check the provider's logs for anything done with the old key since it leaked
Add a secret scanner to CI so the next one is caught before it is pushed
steps.explain: Rotate first: bots scan public repositories within minutes, so deleting the line or rewriting history is too late to be the fix. `git log -p -S'sk_live_' --all` then shows whether other branches hold more copies.

buckets: Key Vault or the platform's secret store
items: Your sandbox payment key on your laptop

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Test every CORS change with a curl preflight, not by reloading the SPA. Keep secrets out of Git from the first commit, and when one leaks, rotate it before anything else. On every endpoint that takes an id, ask in review: where do we check that this user may see this object?
